mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is regarded as 'substitution by dissimilarity of disjunction' (Chandler, n. p)."

Denotation refers to the literal signification or representation between a signifier and the signified.

Locke observed that signs are an important vehicle in communicating 'our thoughts to one another, as well as to record them for our use'.

Pragmatics refers to the relations between signs and their users, that is the effects signs have on the people who use the signs.

Sign is an important term in the definition of semiotics; it is the starting point in semiotic traditions of Saussure and Peirce.

Pictorial Semiotics is the sub-field of semiotics that accounts for how pictures including the various sub- genres of pictures (drawings, paintings, photographs) encode and transmit messages.

The poem is a praise-song dedicated to motherhood for mothers' care and affection.

Langue refers to the rules of language learnt by the user while parole refers to the actual utterances produced by language users.

Rather cognitive semiotics is an approach or model to the study of meaning-making process.

Signs have always been a means of expression from time immemorial.

Cognitive semiotics is the study of how the human minds (including lower animals) interpret meaning.

Natural signs refer to those signs whose basic objective is not to signify, yet lead to the knowledge of something else.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to communicative space which permits free and easy conversations."
Sociopetal space refers to communicative space which permits free and easy conversations.

The syntagmatic plane is the axis of combination of specific signs (by the virtue of the structure of the sign) which occupy particular slots along the horizontal axis.

Referential fallacy is the false assumption that the meaning of a sign is determined by the object to which the sign refers.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a sign which resembles its object in some way; that is it looks or sounds like the object."
Icon is a sign which resembles its object in some way; that is it looks or sounds like the object.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an ideology which sharpens and conceptualises one's way of viewing certain signs within the culture."
Myth is an ideology which sharpens and conceptualises one's way of viewing certain signs within the culture.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a key one in structuralist semiotic analysis."
The distinction is a key one in structuralist semiotic analysis.
